description: Composite of three isothermal phase-section diagrams for quaternary Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys at 900 C. Every panel plots carbon content C (wt%, y-axis, 0-4 with 0.5 ticks) against aluminium content Al (wt%, x-axis, 0-14 with 2 wt% ticks); the panels differ only in manganese level: (a) Mn = 10%, (b) Mn = 20%, (c) Mn = 30%. Each panel overlays up to three line sets: solid black lines calculated with FactSage 6.4 and dotted lines from a CALPHAD approach, plus red lines giving experimentally established isotherms, which appear in (b) and (c) but not in (a). Phase fields are labelled in situ as gamma, gamma+M3C, gamma+kappa, gamma+M3C+kappa, gamma+kappa+alpha, gamma+alpha, alpha+kappa, B2+kappa and kappa. Experimental alloy compositions are marked by open circles, open triangles, open squares, solid squares and solid diamonds; in (a) open circles cluster at Al about 4-8 wt%, C about 0.8-1.5 (gamma field) and open triangles at Al about 10-12 wt%, C about 2.4-3.2 (gamma+kappa); solid squares lie at Al about 8-10 wt%, C below 0.5, and solid diamonds at Al about 12.5-13.5 wt%, C about 1.7-2.2. The figure demonstrates that the three thermodynamic descriptions reproduce the same phase-field topology but diverge in the composition ranges of the gamma, kappa and B2+kappa fields as Mn and Al increase, and that they deviate from the experimental points.

observations.observation: All three panels use the same axes: Al (wt%) from 0 to 14 on the x-axis and C (wt%) from 0 to 4 on the y-axis.
The caption states that (a) is Fe-Mn-Al-C with Mn = 10%, (b) Mn = 20% and (c) Mn = 30%, all as isothermal sections at 900 C.
Red boundary lines (experimentally established isotherms) are visible in panels (b) and (c) but absent from panel (a).

The caption states that solid lines are calculated from FactSage 6.4 and dotted lines are based on a CALPHAD approach, whereas the citing text assigns the dotted lines to Chin et al. [105] and the solid black lines to FactSage [107] - the two reference numbers are in conflict.

The caption states the marker coding: open circle = gamma, open triangle = (gamma+kappa), open square = (gamma+M3C), solid square and solid diamond = the two remaining phase fields, whose printed names (rendered '(alpha+kappa)' and '(c+a)') are partially garbled.
Phase fields labelled inside the panels include gamma, gamma+M3C, gamma+kappa, gamma+M3C+kappa, gamma+kappa+alpha, gamma+alpha, alpha+kappa, B2+kappa and kappa.
In panel (b) solid diamonds are plotted inside the B2+kappa field at Al about 12.5-13.5 wt% and C about 1.7-2.2 wt%.

In panel (a) solid squares sit at the bottom of the diagram at Al about 9-10 wt% with C about 0.1-0.2 wt%, close to the gamma+alpha / alpha+kappa boundary region rather than in a clearly labelled field.
Panel (a) contains no experimental data points in the B2+kappa field or at Al above about 12 wt%.
In panel (c) the red experimental lines enclose a wide gamma+alpha / alpha+kappa wedge around Al about 10-13 wt%, which the black and dotted calculated lines do not reproduce.
Two small black arrows in panel (c) point at neighbouring phase boundaries near Al about 12-13 wt%, illustrating a discrepancy between the line sets.

The citing text states that four phases - ferrite, austenite, cementite and kappa-carbide - exist in the quaternary Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys at hot-working temperatures over the composition range considered.

The citing text states that the experimental data show the gamma region extending toward higher Al concentration as Mn is increased, whereas the calculations give expansion up to 20% Mn and shrinkage beyond it, so calculations deviate from experiment at high Mn and Al.

The citing text states that the experimental points come from Kim et al. [104] in Fig. 7a and Ishida et al. [101] in Fig. 7b and c, while the red isotherms are those of Ishida et al. [102] - a source assignment the caption does not make.

subfigures.description: Isothermal section at 900 C for Mn = 10 wt%, C (wt%) vs Al (wt%). Solid black lines (FactSage 6.4) and dotted lines (CALPHAD) only; no red experimental lines. Labelled fields: gamma+M3C (left), gamma (centre-left, low C), gamma+M3C+kappa (top centre), gamma+kappa (centre-right), gamma+kappa+alpha, alpha+kappa and B2+kappa (far right). Open circles plot in the gamma field, open triangles in gamma+kappa, solid squares at the bottom near Al about 9-10 wt%, C about 0.1-0.2; no points are plotted in B2+kappa.

Isothermal section at 900 C for Mn = 20 wt%. All three line sets present: red experimental isotherms plus solid and dotted calculated boundaries. Fields labelled gamma+M3C, gamma, gamma+M3C+kappa, gamma+kappa, gamma+kappa+alpha, gamma+alpha, alpha+kappa, B2+kappa and kappa (top right). Open squares appear at Al about 2-5 wt%, C about 1.3-2.5 (gamma+M3C), open circles in gamma, open triangles in gamma+kappa, solid squares at Al about 8-10.5 wt%, C about 0-0.5, and solid diamonds in the B2+kappa region at Al about 12.5-13.5 wt%, C about 1.7-2.2.

Isothermal section at 900 C for Mn = 30 wt%. Red experimental lines form a wide triangular wedge (gamma+alpha and alpha+kappa) around Al about 10-13 wt%, cutting across the black and dotted calculated boundaries. Fields labelled gamma+M3C, gamma, gamma+M3C+kappa, gamma+kappa, gamma+kappa+alpha, gamma+alpha, alpha+kappa, B2+kappa and kappa. Open squares sit in gamma+M3C, open circles in gamma, open triangles at Al about 10-12 wt%, C about 1-1.5, and solid diamonds near the B2+kappa field at Al about 12.5-13.5 wt%, C about 1.7-2.2. Two small black arrows annotate boundaries near Al about 12-13 wt%.

unreadable_items: Caption marker legend: the last two field names are rendered '(alpha+kappa)' and '(c+a)'; the '(c+a)' entry is garbled and its true field name could not be read
Panel (c): text of the two small black arrow annotations is not readable at the supplied resolution

Reference numbering conflict between caption ([102,105] for points, [107] for dotted lines) and citing text ([104]/[101] for points, [105] for dotted, [107] for solid) cannot be resolved from the image
Small phase-field labels near the crowded right-hand corner (Al > 12 wt%) are only partially readable
